title: Give the shop a real API
outcome: Run an endpoint with a documented request and response.
story: The website and shop staff need one service for creating messages. Agree on the exact request before connecting the interface.

frames.explanation: The service rejects data that cannot become a useful message.
The client cannot choose server-owned fields.

sections.title: Agree on the boundary
paragraphs: An API lets programs communicate through a contract. POST /messages accepts JSON containing text. A successful response uses 201 and returns a created record. Invalid text uses 422 with a useful explanation.

Keep the contract small: trim outer whitespace, accept 1 to 200 characters, and reject extra fields. The service chooses ids and ownership. Writing examples of accepted and rejected requests prevents frontend and backend from guessing differently.

sections.title: Run a real endpoint
paragraphs: FastAPI maps a Python function to an HTTP method and path. A Pydantic model describes allowed fields and performs runtime validation. The project includes a FastAPI service; start it using the README and open /docs to inspect its generated API documentation.

The browser exercise implements the response decision as a function so you can inspect it quickly. It does not listen on a network port. The project requires actual requests to the running service and verifies response status and JSON.

sections.title: Validate before saving
paragraphs: JSON being syntactically valid does not make its contents acceptable. Check the object shape, field types, and limits before using the database. Trim first, then measure the remaining text. Reject a whitespace-only message.

Validation errors are expected client outcomes. Internal database failures are different; do not turn every exception into a successful empty list. Avoid returning traceback details to customers. Keep diagnostic details in controlled server logs.

sections.title: Prove the contract with requests
paragraphs: Use curl, the API docs, or a small test client to send normal, boundary, and invalid requests. Inspect both HTTP status and body. A response of 201 with the wrong owner is still a bug.

Keep service, data access, and business rules separate enough to test. Use a temporary test database, not a real shop database. Before releasing, document how a client should recover from validation errors and temporary service failures.

words.meaning: An HTTP method and path handled by the service.
The agreed input, output, and failure behaviour.
Checking the values a running program actually receives.

explanation: The function checks the shape before reading text.
Trimming happens before the length rule.
The output includes the status and a predictable body.

exercise.title: Validate a create-message request
exercise.brief: Return a status/body dictionary. Use 201 for a valid trimmed text and 422 for bad requests. The project turns this rule into real HTTP behaviour.

steps.title: Accept a valid message
steps.task: Return trimmed text in a 201 response.
steps.hint: Return exactly status and body; body has only text.

steps.title: Reject invalid text
steps.task: Reject a non-object or non-string text with text must be a string. Reject blank or over-200 text with text must contain 1 to 200 characters.
steps.hint: Check type before calling strip; check length after stripping.

steps.title: Reject extra fields
steps.task: After checking text type, require the only request field to be text. Use unexpected fields for other keys.

cases.label: Text with the wrong type
cases.why: The field must support text operations.

cases.label: Only whitespace
cases.why: Empty content is rejected after trimming.

project.title: A running message service
project.brief: Use the service workspace in the kit to implement and call a FastAPI endpoint backed by SQLite. Add tests before attaching the website.
deliverables: HTTP tests using a temporary database.

milestones.title: Create and retrieve
actions: Validate text with a request model.
Save a valid message using a parameterized statement.
Return 201 and an id chosen by the service.

milestones.title: Test the boundary
actions: Send ordinary, blank, over-limit, and extra-field requests.
Retrieve the saved record after a restart.
Compare each result with the contract.

acceptance: Requests reach a real HTTP service.
Invalid input is rejected before storage.
The test suite uses an isolated database.

tests.expected: 201 with a server-selected id and trimmed text.
